column5: Criterion 7 and C7 dispatch only when the postmaster has room for another run; emitting every READY breaks it.
Ticket never says how readiness is read on a tracker kind with no adapter; several options exist.
Ticket does not reach logging of the readiness result; the existing log-every-action rule requires the logger to accept it.
C4 names only the turnpikes note; the existing every-write-logged rule in trackers.md, not the ticket, requires the other writes logged.
Ticket's same, moved, changed and missing results do not say what a cite past end of file reports.
C5 allows one clerk per ticket; colliding handles across projects wrongly refuse a second project's clerk under any reading.
Criterion 18 fails only a run that started a workhorse before checking premises; a premise-stop run started none.
The ready mark is a label named ready; a single label 'blocked, ready' is not that under any reading.
Criterion 7 requires dispatch with no further word from the user; a path that stalls without a watcher contradicts it.
A failed read must not skip the unmark D4 requires; failing closed is the one sane answer.
Ticket never says what a sign-off covers when the text is edited afterwards; D4 rejected unmarking on any edit.
A corrupted marker must fail closed; reading it as no marker lets a changed ticket pass, which any reading rejects.
C14 states the end result but not how send-back works on a tracker kind where unmark refuses.
A comment after sign-off is not a ticket change; hashing the Log trailer is a wrong comparison under any reading.
Signing off a commented ticket must succeed; the edit base and the adapters' stored-body comparison disagree, wrong under any reading.
The Log-trailer heuristic mis-binds Log-tailed bodies; a wrong comparison any reading rejects, fixed by digesting the stored body.
Ready is a label named ready; a lone comma flag making 'blocked, ready' read ready is wrong under any reading.
Queue and check digest different bodies, so a commented ticket falsely refuses; a wrong comparison under any reading.
Ticket never says what happens when the issue text changes between sign-off and binding; roll-back is one of several options.
Criterion 7's landed predicate includes a provider-reported merged pull request; re-entry after a crash must use it.
Criterion 7 requires the card's check results to match verify.sh results; omitting passing ones violates that.
The runbook's shipped write omits the actor the script requires; wrong against the script, outside the ticket.
Ticket never says how a restart tells a post-landing crash from an interrupted correction.
Ticket never says what a crash between landing and marker removal does on restart.
Criterion 7 requires the default branch to contain HEAD and HEAD not be BASE; an empty branch must not skip.
Ticket says browser suite and QA only where the project has them; which checks are required is unstated.
Criterion 7 lists a provider-reported squash merge as a landed shape; stalling it contradicts the ticket.
Criterion 7 requires card and verify results to match; differing shapes make that comparison impossible.
Card reconciliation labels must match the checkpoint's own vocabulary; a mismatch is wrong under any reading.
Criterion 7 names an empty branch after the default branch moves as a shape that must not count as landed.
Criterion 7 lists a check with no result logged; the ruling judged it a non-pass, so it must be decidable.
Ticket does not define the final states of findings on the card; a ruling asked for explicit ones.
Ticket never says what the landed check does when the provider's pull request head cannot be resolved locally.
Ticket never says what re-verify does when card head and ticket ref differ for a cause other than movement.
C16 compares the waybill's generated Team mode line; a quoted Team heading in ticket text must not be read.
The code's own message requires on or off; a typo silently running lanes unconfined is wrong under any reading.
Existing stdin handling of the dash argument worked before; breaking it is a regression no reading allows.
Criterion 2 covers every step; resolving a subdirectory target to the repository root is the one sane answer.
Criterion 2 and C2 require each launch's limits to follow project settings; the flag placement misses host run.
Ticket never says what a relative env_file is relative to, including with no global config; the user ruled it.
Criterion 3 requires settings to be complete; a legacy-facts-only file is not complete, and the base reported missing config.
Run line calls it a regression from the base; silently dropping the machine's config has one sane answer.
Ticket never says what a relative env_file is relative to; the same choice must reach --run launches.
Criterion 4 gates tracked files on acceptance; failing open when git refuses has one sane answer, failing closed.
Text is only a target and severity line, with no claim about what is wrong.
D1 and D8 stop the run until ruled; a wall lost on log failure must still gate, under any reading.
Reading the repo line from the waybill must handle spaced paths and ignore ticket text; wrong under any reading.
D5 says a reset time is understood only in known shapes, otherwise none; fabricated times contradict it.
D8 stops the run until ruled; an unreadable log reading as no walls must fail closed, the one sane answer.
Ticket does not reach workflow dispatch inputs; interpolating an input into a script is a security fault under any reading.
Ticket never says what the card step does for target repositories without the contract index or checker.
Ticket never says which copy or location names the detector file, or whose version is trusted.
Ticket does not say which copy of the checker a re-check runs, the branch's or the base's.
Criterion 1 says each listed file is covered whole; a region map leaving the entrypoint out contradicts it.
Criterion 4 requires a change to any listed file, wording fixes included, to answer yes; unmapped sentences answer no.
Ticket never says what a re-check does on the branch that introduces the checker, where no base copy exists.
Reporting no change when git could not read is wrong; failing closed is the one sane answer.
Text calls it pre-existing error-path design, which the ticket's change does not reach; criterion 4 covers tool output only.
Ticket never says whether a result event restating the last message prints; several behaviours are reasonable.
Text is only a disposition, dismissed as synthetic-only, with no statement of the behaviour.
Run line shows blank codex text printing as None; wrong output under any reading, same class as M2.
Criterion 5 requires each control to fail on the old behaviour; the N2 control passed on the mutant.
Text is only a disposition, dismissed as synthetic-only, with no statement of the behaviour.
A cleanup must not close a space holding a live launch under any reading; the stale settled state is a defect.
Criterion 2 names a rule that lets only Bubblewrap create namespaces; a user-writable path breaks that.
Truncating the brief's ticket at a heading named Team or Dispatch drops requirements; wrong under any reading of criterion 1.
A stale line pin in an old oracle after an insert is a mismatch with no ticket behaviour behind it.
